result.title: How Far Is Too Far? Object Recognition Declines Monotonically with Semantic Distance
result.summary: Vision models are sensitive to object-background context, yet it remains unclear how recognition changes as the semantic distance between objects and backgrounds increases. We introduce ImageNet-OOC1k, a benchmark enabling graded control of object-background relationships along a continuous consensus visual-semantic dissimilarity axis. This formulation reveals a highly consistent monotonic decline in recognition accuracy across 35 models spanning convolutional neural networks, Vision Transformers, and vision-language models. Internal analyses of Vision Transformers reveal patterns consistent with aggregation failure, where object evidence is present at the patch level but not consolidated into the final prediction. Using this characterization as a diagnostic probe, a simple spatial re-ranking strategy recovers a subset of these errors and improves in-sample accuracy by up to 5.7 percentage points. These results establish context sensitivity as a continuous and predictable property of modern vision systems, with Vision Transformer analyses suggesting that aggregation limitations may contribute to some failure types even when object evidence remains available.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 ImageNet-OOC1k 基准，沿连续的物体-背景语义距离轴分级控制上下文关系，在 35 个 CNN、ViT 与视觉语言模型上发现识别准确率随语义距离单调下降，并借助 ViT 内部探针指出「聚合失败」：证据存在于 patch 层却未汇入最终预测，并用空间重排序部分纠错。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作诊断的「视觉证据存在但未被最终答案使用」与 LVR 关心的视觉旁路、信息坍缩及答案是否真正利用视觉内容高度同构，其 patch 级探针与重排序可供核查能否用于评估多模态模型的 latent 证据筛选与使用。
